To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) highly unsaturated lipophilic drugs and endogenous lipids induce fast inactivation of Kv channels by open‐channel block; (ii) RNA editing in the inner pore cavity modulates drug and lipid binding and thus inactivation; (iii) Kv channels with a different editing pattern are expressed in different brain regions, which can profoundly alter the response of neurons to lipophilic drugs.
RNA editing of Kv1 channels in the brain can alter the binding of drugs, lipids and Kvβ subunit to the pore of these channels.
(1) highly unsaturated fatty acyls induce fast inactivation of Kv1 channels by blocking the open pore; and (2) this inactivation is strongly reduced when editing of the pore cavity is altered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modulation of the gating of voltage‐gated potassium channels by highly unsaturated fatty acid and drugs and the underlying molecular mechanisms.
the molecular mechanisms that determine drug and lipid sensitivity of potassium channels, and the functional significance of RNA editing in the central nervous system.
the regulation of ion channels by RNA editing and the role of this mechanism in drug resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the RNA editing of a single amino acid in Kv1.2 channels, which is located in the pore cavity of the channel protein, results in a change in the kinetics of channel activation and inactivation and a change in the pharmacology of these channels, which can be attributed to the altered interactions with the lipid environment.
RNA editing can modulate the binding of drugs to the open pore and thereby the pharmacology of the Kv channel.
RNA editing of Kv1 channels in the brain can alter the binding of highly unsaturated fatty acid and drugs to the open pore, which in turn can affect neuronal excitability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lipid‐induced fast inactivation of Kv channels represents open‐channel block by lipids, which is strongly reduced in channels that contain edited subunits.
RNA editing can modulate the binding of drugs, highly unsaturated fatty‐acids and Kvβ subunit to the pore of Kv channels.
RNA editing of Kv1.x potassium channel subunits modulates the binding affinity of lipids and drugs to the inner pore cavity of Kv channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNA editing can alter the binding of drugs to Kv channels.
the time course of inactivating Kv potassium channels is an important factor in controlling the firing rate of cells.
RNA editing in Kv1.x potassium channels can profoundly alter the interaction with drugs and lipids.
